# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 53 (Bu-Vb Pc53)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Pācittiya 53 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga establishes the training rule regarding "playing in water" (*hasadhamma*). The regulation stipulates that a monk who plays in or with water commits an offense requiring expiation and confession [Van Gorkom 2009]. Discussing the rationale behind Vinaya rules regulating minute details of daily conduct, modern commentary notes that seemingly innocent behavior such as water play or teasing is motivated by unwholesome states of mind (*akusala citta*) rather than wholesome ones (*kusala citta*) [Van Gorkom 2009].

The rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic codes. Direct parallels exist in the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, along with corresponding nuns' rules such as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 134. DharmaNexus independently identifies cross-language alignments with Tibetan Vinaya literature, including the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), and *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records recurring phraseology shared most extensively with the Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1), the Kosala Saṁyutta (SN 3), and related Vibhaṅga training rules such as Pācittiya 52, 55, and 83 [DharmaNexus].
